nodes.title: How an edit supersedes a landed turn (refines dc-r143-edit-supersedes-landed-grade, 14.4). FULL UNDO, not a correction event. (1) The pre-turn snapshot lives in a new one-row-per-lesson table lesson_undo (lesson_id pk, turn_seq, turn, prev jsonb, ids jsonb), overwritten in the same transaction as each committed turn with a turnSeq, never in lesson.state. (2) The original's evidence-bearing rows are MOVED to archive tables with identical columns plus superseded_by / superseded_at (evidence_superseded, kt_evidence_superseded, …) in the edit's transaction, so no reader needs a filter and no later re-fold can resurrect the abandoned grade. Turn rows stay with meta.superseded. (3) Async writers (blind grader, weave queue, grade_audit) write only while their evidence id is still live, else drop with a trace row. The Conductor gets a turn.superseded event. Misconception counters come from the restored prev plus the live ledger. (4) Only while state.lastAck.turnSeq is the edit's turnSeq; otherwise a turn.edit_missed trace row. Why not the correction event (post the edit as the next turn): when the abandoned value was right and the correction wrong, the Director has moved to the next item, so the edit would be graded against the wrong item or need a rewind anyway. Before building, measure how often a correction actually lands after its turn in voice lessons at today's R. Migration: 4B's DB and TEST only; production at main's deploy after review.
nodes.reversal: the snapshot write costs > 20 ms p95 per turn, or the measured frequency of post-landing corrections is too low to justify the machinery (then the correction-event route with item pinning)

nodes.title: Proposed: a nullable superseded_by column on evidence and kt_evidence, with every reader filtering it. md.decisions:
## dc-r143-edit-full-undo (2026-10-15)

- **What:** a correction that arrives after its turn has landed gets a full undo. The pre-turn snapshot lives in its own one-row-per-lesson table. The abandoned grade's rows move to archive tables, so no reader can bring them back. Background writers check the evidence is still live first. This is 14.4.
- **Why:** posting the correction as the next turn grades it against the wrong question whenever the lesson has already moved on.
- **Reversal:** the snapshot costs more than 20 ms p95 per turn, or such corrections turn out too rare to justify it.
md.rejected:
## rj-r143-supersede-flag-column (2026-10-15)

- **Tried (proposal):** a superseded_by flag on the evidence tables, filtered by every reader.
- **What breaks:** about 10 readers today. Any one that misses the filter, now or later, silently brings back the abandoned grade.
- **Instead:** move superseded rows to archive tables.
